dedupe_keys.name: us wildfire burn zone disasters dataset 2000 to 2025

description: This dataset identifies wildfire burn zone disasters in the United States, where burn zones came near or into wildland-urban interface communities to the point of a disaster, by harmonising six wildfire datasets, and gives each one a spatial footprint so exposure of people and infrastructure can be studied consistently. It covers 2000 to 2025, with 6,212 disasters drawn from 6,871 candidate wildfires; 2,392 have mapped fire perimeters, 3,697 use buffers around a point and 123 are points only. It was produced by L. B. Wilner, L. Piepmeier, J. A. Casey and co-authors and described in Scientific Data in December 2025. The data are available for download from Harvard Dataverse (version 4, released September 2025) as a GeoJSON file of about 326 MB with a data dictionary, under CC0 1.0 and free of charge; a lighter GitHub repository with code is released under MIT. Caveats: disasters without mapped perimeters are represented by buffers or points, which overstate or understate the area affected. It supports hazard exposure, cascading impact and recovery studies linking wildfires to buildings, power, water and health services at the wildland-urban interface; a related record is the Forest Service building loss and rebuilding data.
